Subject: BrightLane - post-demo recap & quickstart asks

Hi Olivia — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and three asks so we can scope hosted vs dedicated: 

Recap (2-minute):
- Use-case: real-time summarization + 1-step classification for knowledge search results (latency sensitive, 95th pct target ~ 200ms).
- Peak pattern you mentioned: a bursty storefront event (payment/checkout spikes) with ~800 qps for ~10–20 minutes, baseline ~30 qps.
- Data residency: US-only; no current plan for on-prem.

Recommended immediate path: start with Hosted API pilot (fast onboarding) + endpoint partitioning and KV prefix caching to reduce tokens on common prompts. We flagged a potential switch to Dedicated if sustained sustained QPS > ~500 for >24h or if you need strict network isolation.

Asks:
1) Could you share a realistic 48-hour traffic profile (UTC) with percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and typical avg token count per request?
2) Any requirements on private networking / VPC or is a managed-hosted endpoint acceptable?
3) Who will own SOC2/compliance intake so we can send the questionnaire?

Attachments: demo recording + quickstart steps (links in body).

Next steps I propose: deliver quickstart sandbox credentials, map 2 logical endpoints (search-summ, search-rerank) and set initial ratecaps, then run a 48h pilot.

Best,
Ben

Hi Olivia / Carlos — thanks for the quick reply, happy to clarify. Short answers up front, details below.

TL;DR: Hosted endpoints are mapped to logical route buckets; you get per-endpoint ratecaps and an account-level safety ceiling. Prefix/KV caching lowers token counts (and thus billing) — we track effective token-saved metrics in the Console so you can see a reduced effective token-per-call and lower billed tokens.

Mapping and rate model (practical):
- We recommend creating 2 endpoints for your pilot: /search-summ (generation-heavy) and /search-rerank (embedding/rerank). Each endpoint gets an independent ratecap in the hosted sandbox so you can tune separately.
- Account safety ceiling prevents runaway cost (we set a conservative default, which you can raise).
- Example starting caps for pilot: /search-summ = 120 req/s (burst to 250 for short windows), /search-rerank = 250 req/s, account ceiling = 600 req/s. These are adjustable during pilot.

Caching & billing:
- Prefix/KV caching reduces tokens billed: cached prefixes avoid re-generation; we surface a "tokens_saved" metric per endpoint in Console. Billing is on tokens consumed post-cache.

Dedicated trigger guidance:
- Typical threshold: if you have a sustained 24h average > 500 req/s on a single endpoint or if you need private networking (VPC peering / on-prem), we recommend moving to Dedicated. For your described pattern (short spikes to 800 qps but baseline low), Hosted with endpoint partitioning + burst policies should be fine.

Operational suggestions for the 48-hour pilot:
- We'll provision two sandbox endpoints and pre-warm KV cache with top 20 common prompts.
- Canary policy: route 10% traffic to a secondary variant for 6h to validate latency and quality.
- Observability: we'll enable token-level breakdown and a 1-min latency dashboard.

Attachments: I attached an endpoint mapping CSV that shows suggested logical routes and initial ratecaps. Also adding a Drive link with a concise runbook.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Olivia: share the 48-hour traffic profile (UTC) + confirm who will own SOC2 intake.
2) Redwood (Prio): provision sandbox endpoints, share credentials and quickstart steps.
3) Marissa: we will schedule a 30m ops preflight with your infra team to discuss peering if Carlos flags a need.

If that sounds good, Ben / Priyom / Marissa and I will coordinate the sandbox provisioning tomorrow.

Best,
